name: Banon, the Returners' Leader
oracle_text:
Pray — Once during each of your turns, you may cast a creature spell from among cards in your graveyard that were put there from anywhere other than the battlefield this turn.
Whenever you attack, you may pay {1} and discard a card. If you do, draw a card.
blocked_sentences: Pray — Once during each of your turns, you may cast a creature spell from among cards in your graveyard that were put there from anywhere other than the battlefield this turn.

needs.what: a static ability that grants its controller permission to cast *other* cards from their own graveyard, with a filter naming which cards qualify (here `types: ["Creature"]`) -- the Muldrotha/Karador/Gisa and Geralf shape
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `play_lands_from_graveyard` is the only graveyard-casting permission in `static_effects`, and it is hard-wired to the land drop: `legality.py` reads it through `player_plays_lands_from_graveyard` solely to widen the land-play action, so it can neither be pointed at creature spells nor at casting at all. The `cast_from_graveyard` in `condition_keys` is not a permission -- it reads the `cast_from_graveyard` flag the stack sets on a spell, and the loader refuses it on any card without its own `flashback`, so it only ever asks about the source card itself, never about other cards in the yard

needs.what: a per-turn use limit on such a casting permission -- "Once during each of your turns" must let exactly one qualifying spell be cast per turn of the permission's controller, and the used-up state must reset each turn
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `set_turn_flag`/`has_turn_flag` can record that something happened this turn, but they are effect ops and conditions readable only while an ability resolves; nothing consults them when legality enumerates castable spells, so there is no way to make a standing permission stop offering itself after its first use

needs.what: a selector key over graveyard cards that matches only those put there this turn, and that can further restrict which zone they came from ("from anywhere other than the battlefield") -- i.e. the engine must remember, per card now in a graveyard, the turn it arrived and the zone it arrived from
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn` is the only this-turn graveyard fact the engine keeps, and `values.py` returns `ledger.cards_to_graveyard`, a bare integer across all graveyards -- it retains neither which cards arrived nor where they came from. No key in `selector_keys` reads arrival time or previous zone, so a graveyard selector can only see the whole yard, which would let this ability recur a creature that died in combat five turns ago
